races.name: Sporting Times EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Valdoro
runners_data.note: Dropped back to minimum 5f after two sixth-place efforts at 6f on Good ground; De Sousa booking for a small progressive yard is positive, and as the natural front-runner from stall 3 he can dictate on his own terms — sim-going record reads 2/2 which at least shows no going concern.

runners_data.name: Ivory Moon
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f on Soft for Boughey with Loughnane aboard — the form is strong and the step up in ground to Good is the key unknown; races in midfield by inclination but the light field means she has been pushed back positionally in the map, so her winning chance relies on the pace duel softening the leaders rather than her closing from a natural rear position.

runners_data.name: Perfect Strike
runners_data.note: Two consecutive seventh-place finishes at 6f on Good ground for Haggas suggest little improvement has been found, and shortening to 5f could help or simply mean he gets beaten sooner; as the second confirmed front-runner from stall 4, he will have to commit early and burn against Valdoro, which makes him a pace facilitator as much as a winning threat.

runners_data.name: Warriors Chant
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Gary & Moore from stall 5 with no public form to assess; style listed as unknown and going unknown — entirely dependent on raw ability and how quickly Jason Watson can find cover or position in the first furlong.

runners_data.name: Sinova
runners_data.note: Another debut runner, this time from Richard Hannon's yard from the outside stall 7 — Hannon's 14-day strike rate of 2/47 gives little statistical encouragement, and from stall 7 on a 5f track there is the least room for error out of the gate; style and going flags unknown.

runners_data.name: Igrok
runners_data.note: Tenth and seventh in two starts at 6f and 5f on Good ground, both midfield efforts that went nowhere; a 74-day layoff for a Stuart Williams-trained juvenile makes improvement hard to project, and his profile does not scream immediate relevance in a sprint dominated by front-runners.

runners_data.name: Rapid Deployment
runners_data.note: Two modest efforts at 6f on Good ground for Beckett, placing fifth and seventh; 55 days since last run and a midfield style mean he needs the pace duel to extract itself before the final furlong, which is plausible but not the most likely shape given Valdoro's likely control.

races.paceDynamic: Valdoro and Perfect Strike are the two confirmed front-runners in a seven-runner field, and with both drawn centrally (stalls 3 and 4) they will lock horns from the gate, creating a genuinely contested pace over this sharp Sandown 5f. That rivalry is unlikely to produce a suicidal gallop but should generate an honest, even tempo that stretches the field out early and removes any chance of a slow-run tactical affair. Midfielders Rapid Deployment, Igrok and the redistributed Ivory Moon will need to pick through traffic if the pace-setters don't tie each other up, but on Good ground over 5f Sandown rewards horses with early toe and the ability to sustain speed — not closers who need a late collapse. The race shape heavily favours a front-running or at worst prominent profile; the field holds more pace-committed horses than can all secure their preferred position, with Valdoro (inside draw, proven willingness) most likely to control the rail and Perfect Strike forced to match or be outpaced early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Valdoro Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Valdoro asserts from the gate and Perfect Strike cannot sustain the early duel, gifting Valdoro an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Valdoro has already shown a willingness to front-run at 6f on Good ground and dropping to 5f at Sandown — where early position is premium — plays to that style; with Perfect Strike potentially beaten for toe or pressure, Valdoro can dictate a rhythm that suits his profile and hold on under De Sousa's hands-and-heels finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Blows Up
scenarios.trigger: If both Valdoro and Perfect Strike fight hard throughout, leaving both vulnerable late.
scenarios.body: A contested lead over a sharp 5f on Good ground can drain both pace-setters before the final furlong, opening the door for a horse that travels just off the pace or possesses a superior finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Warriors Chant or Sinova — both making their debut — show natural raw speed to take advantage of an honest gallop.
scenarios.body: Unknown quantities with no public form can occasionally exploit a set pace when possessing untapped ability, and Moore or Hannon sending out a first-timer in a novice with a clear shape at least gives structure to attack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Mop Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually strong and the front two exhaust each other, allowing the genuine hold-up horses to swoopfrom the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because Ivory Moon — the most credentialed hold-up type — is a redistributed midfield horse rather than a true closer, meaning the closing threat is structurally weak; Rapid Deployment and Igrok have not shown the required finishing burst from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Valdoro and Perfect Strike are both confirmed front-runners from adjacent stalls 3 and 4 — watch the first two furlongs for which horse blinks first; if Valdoro is allowed to stride clear unchallenged, this race could be over very early.

Ivory Moon's going switch from Soft debut to Good today is unproven — if the ground rides faster than expected she may struggle to replicate her debut win, despite Boughey/Loughnane being a potent combination.
Both debutants Warriors Chant (stall 5) and Sinova (stall 7) carry a blanket of unknown — if either shows unusual early speed they could disrupt the projected pace map entirely without warning.

Perfect Strike has failed to place in two starts and arrives as the second front-runner likely to be outgunned by Valdoro early; his failure to land even a place on either start suggests he is more of a pace-injection tool than a genuine winner in this contest.

Igrok's 74-day absence for Stuart Williams — a trainer who operates at 6/24 over 14 days — means fitness and freshness are worth monitoring in the paddock; if he shows any ring-rustiness he will struggle to be competitive from midfield in a fast-run 5f.

races.name: Visit Sri Lanka Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Isle Of Lismore
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old in good recent form (won last time at Good going over 5f) for Robert Cowell, with Billy Loughnane's experienced hands an asset from stall 1; prominent style should see him close to the pace early but will need to navigate a congested group of similar types.|

runners_data.name: On Edge
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground recently and has the going profile to be competitive (2W from 6 Good-ground runs in this form cycle), but draw 9 and Ashley Lewis's claim may not fully compensate for being asked to hold a prominent position in a very busy early pack.|

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's lead danger — a three-year-old hold-up type whose sole win came over 5f on Good ground and whose trainer Gary & Josh Moore have two winners from 26 recent runners; Toby Moore's 7lb claim helps the weight, and the race shape created by front-runners fighting suits this style directly.|

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection — a confirmed front-runner who has won over this exact trip and going combination for Stuart Williams (6 winners from 24 in the last 14 days); the concern is Always Perfect's presence, meaning Merrimack cannot dictate freely, which introduces the low-confidence tag, but the horse remains central to how this race is run.|

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: Straightforward form figures over 5f on Good ground (placed once from 15 visits) for Charlie Wallis, with a negligible T14 strike rate; though a natural prominent racer, the abundance of pace-seeking types in this field means Lazzar is highly likely to find itself racing further back than its preference, blunting its chance.|

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with three placed efforts from 11 Good-ground runs over this trip, handled capably by Silvestre De Sousa from stall 3; prominent style could find a slot just off the early leaders if the two front-runners monopolise the very head of affairs, making this horse a natural each-way shape beneficiary.|

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Two wins from 12 Good-ground starts over 5f and 6f for Stuart Williams — same yard as Merrimack — with Marco Ghiani aboard; a prominent type whose form figures of 1-2-2 in recent handicap company show she travels well to the line when not overexposed at the front.|

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Three-year-old confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Good going over this distance; Charlie Fellowes has only one winner from 15 recent runners so stable form is modest, but Always Perfect's bold jumping style means it will be directly involved in shaping the race from the first stride and cannot be ignored on pace grounds.|

runners_data.name: Moe's Legacy
runners_data.note: A midfield runner on 7d turnaround for R Harris (no winners in the last 14 days), carrying top weight of 138lbs; form figures of 2-2 in Good-going placed efforts suggest a horse that can get involved late, but the weight burden and short turnaround add risk on what is already a competitive flat sprint.|

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Richard Hannon (modest 2/47 T14 strike) ridden by Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim; has placed three times on Good ground without winning and drops in from 6f, so the 5f and sprint pace scenario could suit if the front-runners empty themselves — but the winless record on Good turf is a persistent concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Merrimack and Always Perfect are confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested early pace over this 5f on Good turf at Sandown — neither is likely to concede without a battle. Behind them, Isle Of Lismore, On Edge, Hint Of Humour, and Adalida all want prominent positions, generating a congested group of four chasing that early berth and raising the risk of traffic interference and checking between the 2f and 3f markers. This field contains more pace-seeking types than can all find their natural position, with Lazzar — a genuine prominent racer — most likely squeezed into a midfield role it would not normally occupy, reducing its chance of striking at the right moment. The contested early gallop and prominent congestion favour runners who can settle just off the lead without burning fuel, and closers with a genuine late kick stand to benefit if the duel up front burns both protagonists out — however, the tactical verdict leans toward hold-up horses with strong finishing kicks, particularly Havana Smile, as the pace is set by others and the Good going should allow that profile to land a late blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Merrimack and Always Perfect fight each other to the line, setting a true pace that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: The duel between Merrimack and Always Perfect produces an honest gallop that leaves both vulnerable late, as neither can dominate cleanly and one or both fade inside the final furlong. Hold-up horses with a genuine finishing kick, especially Havana Smile, receive the ideal setup as the pace dissolves in front of them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Merrimack breaks fastest and takes full command, dictating an even gallop that suits its pattern.
scenarios.body: Merrimack, with the benefit of Stuart Williams's in-form yard and a solid recent record over this trip and going, sets a measured tempo that drains the finish from closers and rewards its own sustained gallop. Always Perfect may track closely but cannot deliver a decisive late challenge if the pace is metronomic rather than brutal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to weaken the leaders but a close-tracking horse times the run perfectly from second or third.
scenarios.body: Adalida or Hint Of Humour, travelling comfortably just off the leaders, gain maximum momentum at the 1f pole as the front two start to tire, hitting the line before the closers can fully wind up their challenges. Good going suits this profile and both horses have consistent placed form at this trip, making them natural beneficiaries of a honest-but-not-scorching gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace moderates unexpectedly and front-runners are allowed a soft lead that preserves their energy late.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race that benefits hold-up types on paper instead traps them with too much ground to make up in the final furlong on a tight 5f at Sandown, leaving them finishing into the places at best. Merrimack or Always Perfect, coasting to an easy lead, conserve enough to hold on as Havana Smile and Cayman Tai find the winning post arriving too soon.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a battle between Merrimack and Always Perfect at the break — if either is knocked sideways or forced wide from stalls 8 and 2, the early dynamics change completely and the whole field's positioning may be compromised.

The prominent congestion involving Isle Of Lismore, On Edge, Hint Of Humour, and Adalida creates a real risk of interference between the 3f and 2f markers as riders jostle for the rail — any horse forced to check or switch will lose critical momentum.

Lazzar will very likely fail to secure its preferred prominent berth given the volume of pace-seeking runners ahead of it in the betting; watch whether Joe Leavy opts to drop in and ride for luck or forces the issue, as either choice carries risk.

Havana Smile's hold-up profile means Toby Moore (7lb claimer) needs a clean passage through the final furlong — with 10 runners and a pace-strung-out field, any pocket of horses at the 1f pole could cost the Strand Scorecard's danger dearly.

Moe's Legacy arrives on a 7-day turnaround carrying 138lbs — watch the market to see if there is a market move suggesting a specific fitness angle, as a flat or drifting price would be a significant flag against its chance in this competitive sprint.

races.name: Sporting Times/sri Lanka Awaits You Ebf Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)
Sporting Times/sri Lanka Nursery Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Norham
runners_data.note: Trained by Adam Kirby (0/5 in 14 days) and ridden by Cieren Fallon; won over 7f at Sandown last time before a drop back to 5f, and this return to a mile looks well-judged — prominent style suits a true-pace race and the going is confirmed Good all day.

runners_data.name: Clive The Writer
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a soft 7th at Goodwood then a big-field Sandown win over 7f, and Silvestre De Sousa picks up the ride; naturally inclined to race in midfield and will likely get a clear passage from draw 7 if the front-runners tie each other up.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Burgundy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Richard Hannon sending him on a 50-day break, suggesting some freshening was needed; drew 5 and will have to be committed early, and if Cilician burns him from gate 1 the 7f winner may find the extra furlong a test of his stamina under that pressure.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Bent
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form, winning last time out over 6f on Good ground, and Dylan Cunha's yard is in fair nick (2/24); wears headgear and is a prominent type who should travel smoothly off the pace-setters without getting embroiled in the duel — the step to a mile is the one open question.

runners_data.name: Drum Bay
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has been firing well (9/45 in 14 days) and this horse has placed twice in its two career starts, both at longer trips including 8f on Good; runs in the prominent group naturally and the Sandown flat mile suits a stayer-in-waiting.

runners_data.name: Tiora Time
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's filly carries a strong form profile — winner over 6f, placed twice over 7f on Good going — and Neil Callan gets the ride; she is a genuine prominent racer who is compressed into an apparent midfield position purely because this field is loaded with pace-committed types, so do not treat her as a hold-up horse in race-reading.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard flags as a danger and Brian Meehan sends him back just 14 days after his last run; six starts on Good ground with three placings shows genuine consistency, and from draw 1 Billy Loughnane can slot onto the rail and lead or press — the highest OR in the field at 84 reflects real ability but recent form (4th, 8th) carries some caution.

runners_data.name: Crown Ranger
runners_data.note: Marco Botti (5/15 in 14 days) and Marco Ghiani combine for this 3rd-last-time-out horse who is a natural prominent racer by inclination; he is shown at the rear of the map only because the field's pace glut leaves no room — his chances depend heavily on whether he can find a position closer to the speed than his mapped slot implies.

races.paceDynamic: Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy are confirmed front-runners and both will be pressing for the lead from the off at Sandown's mile, with draw positions 1 and 5 respectively meaning neither has a natural gate advantage to steal a march — expect a contested, honest gallop rather than a dawdle. Whiskey Bent and Norham will be tracking close behind, compressing the prominent group and ensuring the early sectionals are genuine on this flat Good ground. The result is a race run at a true pace from flag to finish, which classically benefits horses who can travel comfortably in midfield and produce a sustained, rather than explosive, late run — a profile that suits Tiora Time and Drum Bay more than it suits the lead-duellers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Cilician (draw 1) and Duke Of Burgundy (draw 5) are best placed to actually lead, while Crown Ranger and Tiora Time are likely to be pushed wider in the pack than they would choose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy burn each other off at an honest gallop and the prominent pack is strung out by halfway.
scenarios.body: The front two set a true pace that gradually stretches their stamina reserves over Sandown's flat mile, leaving the race open for a sustained finisher to reel them in through the final two furlongs. Horses who travel comfortably just off the speed without expending energy early are prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician uses draw 1 to break smartly and steals a length or two, forcing Duke Of Burgundy to chase rather than lead freely.
scenarios.body: Cilician has strong recent prominent form with multiple placed efforts at this trip and going, and if allowed even a sliver of daylight could control the fractions and grind rivals into submission. Billy Loughnane riding from a handy draw is a significant asset if the horse pins its ears back early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard too soon and capitulate in the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up types to scythe through.
scenarios.body: Crown Ranger, though genuinely a prominent type rather than a natural hold-up horse, is mapped to the rear and could accidentally benefit if the pace is truly suicidal and gap materialises late. Clive The Writer, drawn 7 and shown as midfield, might be the more honest closer in this shape given a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If a single prominent type tracks the leaders without getting involved in the duel and simply outlasts them in a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: Norham has strong staying form at 7f already and stepping to a mile with Cieren Fallon in the plate could suit a horse that found more when given room; Whiskey Bent is in career-best form having just won and won't stop running either.

watchPoints.text: Cilician vs Duke Of Burgundy — watch the first two furlongs for which leads and at what clip; if both fight for supremacy the race could be run at a pace that compromises both their finishing efforts.

Tiora Time's draw (2) sits between Cilician (1) and Duke Of Burgundy (5) — Neil Callan will need to decide inside the first half-furlong whether to push forward or drop back, and a crowded traffic scenario through the first bend is a real possibility.

Crown Ranger is drawn 8 on the outside and while that avoids inner traffic, Marco Ghiani will need to find cover quickly or face a solo prominent position that burns this horse's energy earlier than ideal.

Whiskey Bent wears headgear and steps from 6f to a mile for the first time; watch its early-race manners and whether it travels kindly in the prominent group or pulls against Jason Watson, as a hard-puller over this longer trip could fade in the straight.

Going is confirmed Good for all seven races at Sandown today with no variance — no ground edge applies to any runner, meaning form, fitness and positioning will be the decisive factors rather than any surface preference.

races.name: Sri Lanka Paradise Island Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Richard Hannon, 27 days since last run and wearing a hood (hg:b); has been consistent without winning in similar conditions (0W2P sim-going across 13 attempts) and is drawn neutrally in stall 3, but six recent starts without a win and a tendency to finish fourth or fifth makes him a vulnerable betting proposition.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Midfield operator from stall 6 for Ian Williams and Billy Loughnane; won from three comparable Good-ground outings but also ran 11th and 14th on Soft, so the confirmed Good going here is genuinely important — his 135lb burden is the highest in the race and a significant impost at this level.

runners_data.name: Zabeel Alkabeir
runners_data.note: The sole pace-maker here, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) signals he is racing in a slightly unfamiliar role; he returns off a 71-day break for Gary & Josh Moore, and while his record shows he has led and won before, the layoff combined with the style caveat tempers confidence in him lasting home.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' four-year-old is lightly raced for the stable with 3 wins from 18 runners over 14 days, holds strong recent form (321 in last three), and has a hard-earned placing record over this trip and 8f on Good — Marco Ghiani rides from the inside stall 1, which suits a horse who will drop in and look for a run late.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard selection at low confidence; James Fanshawe's four-year-old has won and placed twice in four outings on similar Good ground over 7f, and his progressive profile (won over this trip, placed on this surface) gives Cieren Fallon a legitimate platform — the 'low confidence' tag reflects open handicap uncertainty rather than a form concern.

runners_data.name: Sea Founder
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner is rated OR=79, the lowest in the field, giving him a weight advantage; drawn in stall 2 he is well placed to track Zabeel Alkabeir prominently, but his sim-going record on Good turf is strikingly poor (0W0P in one attempt) compared to his better efforts on Stalls or softer ground, which is a notable negative flag.

races.paceDynamic: Zabeel Alkabeir is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner handicap over Sandown's 7f on Good turf, with Sea Founder likely to press from draw 2 and provide early company without seriously disputing the lead. With only two forward-biased horses and no genuine pace battle, Zabeel Alkabeir should control a comfortable, metronomic tempo that neither burns out the leader nor fully charges up the closers. Philanthropist and Huscal, both hold-up types with strong recent form, will need that pace to be genuinely honest enough to reel in the front two from midfield or behind — a steady gallop risks leaving them with too much ground to make up. This shape ultimately favours prominent or early-travelling types who can sit just behind the pace and pounce, though if the tempo proves genuinely fair, late closers with finishing kicks will not be entirely out of it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Zabeel Alkabeir dictates an uncontested, sustainable pace and the closers cannot generate enough momentum on Good ground to collar him late.
scenarios.body: Zabeel Alkabeir sets a metronomic fractions from the front with Sea Founder tracking in second, and the small field gives the hold-up horses a compressed run without the true gallop they need; the race is effectively won in the middle stages before the closers wind up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Powerfully
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely honest and the straight provides enough of a test for Sandown 7f to allow hold-up horses to reel in the front pair.
scenarios.body: Philanthropist — the Strand Scorecard selection with the strongest sim-going profile (1W2P on Good, won on this trip and surface) — would be ideally positioned to come through midfield, with Huscal offering a comparable late threat from draw 1 having placed five times in nine comparable outings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Romp
scenarios.trigger: If Zabeel Alkabeir — racing on a 71-day break and tagged with a STYLE_FIT caveat — sets too strong a gallop and fades abruptly in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Huscal's proven finishing kick (won at 7f on Stalls, placed twice at 8f on Good) would be at a premium, and Philanthropist's consistent proximity on similar ground means both could sweep past a weakening front group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Founder tracks the pace conspicuously close and the race develops slowly enough that a prominent horse can quicken from just off the leader.
scenarios.body: Sea Founder has placed twice at 7f on Stalls-style going and would benefit most from a dawdle-then-sprint scenario, though his limited Good-turf sim-going record (0W0P in one similar attempt) is a genuine worry; Philanthropist stalking from midfield on a stronger pace-driven version of this shape also fits.

watchPoints.text: Zabeel Alkabeir's 71-day absence is the single biggest race-shape risk — if he blows up early or is sluggish to stride, the entire pace map collapses and the closers will be unleashed far earlier than anticipated.

Sea Founder's pitch from stall 2 is worth monitoring at the start — if he pushes up aggressively to join Zabeel Alkabeir, the front-end tempo could rise faster than the lone-leader scenario assumes, opening the door for Huscal and Philanthropist.

Huscal's draw in stall 1 on a track where inside draw is neutral — if he gets shuffled back on the turn into Sandown's straight, Marco Ghiani will need to commit early to avoid losing ground on a horse whose finishing kick is his primary weapon.

The Angel King carries the top weight of 135lbs and has two soft-ground blots in his recent history — confirm he handles the confirmed Good surface fluently in the first two furlongs before treating him as a live runner off his 2/7f/GOO placing.

Philanthropist's headgear (hg:p, a hood/visor) is worth noting as a form flag — horses wearing such equipment for the first time or after a significant absence can show a markedly different running pattern, and Cieren Fallon's tactical deployment could shift the midfield picture.

races.name: Sri Lanka Wonder Of Asia Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance, and good ground last time (1/7f/GOO) and has strong sim-going form; natural prominent style suits this race shape well and Darragh Keenan's booking adds confidence — one of the best-placed of the crowd tracking Gesayed.

runners_data.name: Gesayed
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner from stall 1 with Billy Loughnane aboard; the 83-day absence is a question, but K.R. Burke's 13/42 14-day strike rate shows the yard fires fresh horses — she controls tempo entirely if she breaks cleanly.

runners_data.name: Vanilla Skies
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly with three consecutive placed efforts over 7f on good ground including a win — solid profile, but her natural prominent style cannot be accommodated cleanly in this field with so many rivals competing for that position, and she may find herself further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground on latest start and has been placed in all three career runs at this trip; Ed Walker fires 6/42 in 14 days and Ashley Lewis claims 3lb — a natural prominent type who can realistically slot just off Gesayed and is well-suited to this exact scenario.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: The Strand scorecard's top selection at low confidence; has won twice over 7f on good ground and carries strong recent form (123121), but like Vanilla Skies, is a natural prominent type who is likely to be displaced from her preferred position in this traffic — Callum Hutchinson will need to adapt.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Top-rated on OR at 82 and has placed twice over 8f on good ground, but is a hold-up horse stepping back from longer trips; genuine closer who benefits only if Gesayed sets a strong enough gallop — her form this season shows consistency without getting her head in front.

runners_data.name: Souffler
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground (1/7f/GOO) but that was followed by a weak run on Standard ground (6/7f/STA); natural prominent type who may actually secure a pitch just off Gesayed from stall 2 — more realistic positionally than the redistibuted runners and worth noting with Benoit de la Sayette riding.

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Recent form is uninspiring (227646) and she has not won in five runs; a naturally prominent type who is among those least likely to secure her preferred early berth in this crowded pace scenario, and Jonathan Portman's 1/19 14-day record does not inspire confidence either.

races.paceDynamic: Gesayed breaks from stall 1 as the sole confirmed front-runner and is likely to stride into a clear lead uncontested, setting a sustainable gallop over Sandown's flat seven furlongs on good ground. With no genuine pace rival willing or able to match her from the gates, she will control tempo from the front and avoid any energy-sapping early battle. Behind her, Lyra Lea and Dream Vega are the most natural prominent types able to actually slot into the positions just off the pace, with Souffler also capable of tracking from a handy pitch. Critically, Vanilla Skies, Brisk Symphony, and Allegrino are all true prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred early positions in this traffic — the more likely result is that at least one or two of them are shuffled back from their natural role, which undermines their chance and hands the race shape advantage squarely to genuine hold-up and tracking types who can strike off a measured, single-pacemaker gallop: in particular, front-runners who dictate and closers who produce a single sustained challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gesayed Dictates, Catches All
scenarios.trigger: If Gesayed bowls along uncontested and the gallop is honest enough that hold-up horses can close but not fast enough to peg back a freshly-set leader.
scenarios.body: Gesayed leads at her own pace from stall 1, conserving energy through the middle stages and kicking again entering the final two furlongs; horses who track closely, like Lyra Lea and Dream Vega, are best placed to challenge but may find the leader holding on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Line
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and the tracking runners closest to Gesayed — Lyra Lea and Dream Vega — have enough in reserve to overhaul her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo through the middle turns this into a sprint finish from three out, where horses racing just off the leader hold the decisive advantage over those further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Gesayed sets a genuinely strong, honest gallop that strings the field out and leaves the leaders vulnerable deep inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Distant Shore and any displaced prominent type forced to race off the pace get a genuine tow into the race off a searching tempo; Distant Shore's form at this trip on good ground makes her the most credible beneficiary among the hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early order collapses mid-race due to competing prominent types crowding each other out and pace collapses in the straight.
scenarios.body: With multiple genuine prominent types jostling for position — Brisk Symphony, Vanilla Skies, Allegrino all racing out of role — a muddled race can produce an unpredictable finish where a horse freshly returning or with a recent win finds space at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Vanilla Skies or Brisk Symphony attempt to push forward from their outside draws (7 and 5) — if they contest the early lead with Gesayed, the pace quickens materially and changes the entire race shape.

Allegrino's low-confidence top selection status needs caveating: if she is shuffled back from her natural prominent role by a traffic-heavy early order, her chance is compromised before the race has truly begun.

Gesayed's 83-day absence from the track is the single biggest variable — if she is ring-rusty early and loses her lead, there is no second pacemaker to take over and the race shape collapses into confusion.

Distant Shore is the most straightforward hold-up beneficiary if pace is genuinely honest, but her inability to win in five career runs at various trips suggests she finds ways to be beaten even when the scenario fits.

Dream Vega's claims look solid on paper — three runs, three at 7f good, one win — and she looks the most likely horse to sit second or third behind Gesayed in a position that genuinely suits the probable race shape.

races.name: Sporting Times Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has placed twice over 10f on good ground recently and arrives here fresh on 14 days' rest; this trip and going suit, and while its natural inclination is to race from off the pace — meaning it will sit towards the rear rather than the mapped hold-up zone — the honest pace suits it well, and it merits respect as a Strand scorecard danger.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner with two wins over 10f on good ground and solid form figures at this trip; Ed Walker sends it here on 27 days' rest and it will contest for the early lead directly with Royal Poetry and Plan C, making it a key pace-shape driver rather than a betting proposition on its own merits.

runners_data.name: Tipsy Tiger
runners_data.note: Five-year-old veteran returning from a 74-day absence under William Stone's low-volume yard and wearing a hood; a hold-up type with placed efforts on soft and good-to-soft ground, though the good ground is fine — the layoff and lack of recent competitive action is the main risk here.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old has the form figures of a horse that rarely threatens — no wins, no places in five runs in similar going — and its true hold-up style is being compressed forward on the map because of the pace volume ahead; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations, and the visor may help but is not transformational given the overall profile.

runners_data.name: Plan C
runners_data.note: An Alan King front-runner returning from 91 days off, with placed form over 8f on soft but limited evidence over this trip and good ground; the layoff is significant and it will be doing well to match the pace and fitness of Royal Poetry or Del Corso from the front, making it a pace contributor rather than a likely winner.

runners_data.name: Dancing Tiger
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old arrives 11 days fresh wearing blinkers and has placed twice over 12f on soft and good ground; its genuine running style is hold-up, though in this race its true position will be further back than the map shows, and the medium confidence top pick from the Strand scorecard must deliver a clean passage through a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old is the highest-rated runner in the field at OR 80 and has won and placed repeatedly over 12f on good ground; a genuine front-runner who will push straight to the lead from stall one, it sets the tempo for everyone else, and its stamina credentials are the best among the pace-setters.

runners_data.name: Letmebetheboss
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is a midfield type with a wide draw in stall eight and arrives on 16 days' rest; it won over 14f on soft last time out which raises questions about whether good ground over 10f is truly ideal, and the apprentice rider Myla Coppins needs a clean trip and a genuine pace collapse to get competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong, honest gallop from the outset over 1m2f on good ground at Sandown — a flat, unrelenting track that exposes anything lacking stamina or resolution. With three horses fighting for the same real estate early, the pace will not be manufactured or artificial; it will be genuine and sustained, placing a premium on stamina, class, and the ability to absorb a searching tempo before delivering a finishing effort. This shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield types who can settle behind the battle, then pick off a tiring lead — horses who switch off in the early stages and deliver late will be most advantaged. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear: Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are both genuine hold-up horses redistributed forward on the map because of the sheer volume of pace in this race, but Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso are overwhelmingly more likely to actually secure the front positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso ignite a genuine early battle and the race is truly end-to-end, leaving the field strung out and tiring.
scenarios.body: The three confirmed front-runners burn each other off through the early and middle stages, handing the advantage to any runner who has settled and conserved energy before unleashing a sustained run from the home turn; Sandown's flat, relentless finish rewards those with genuine staying power over sprint-finishing ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Del Corso or Royal Poetry gets a softer lead than expected after one of the front-runners drops out early, allowing a controlled tempo that benefits the best-placed horse.
scenarios.body: A more moderate gallop than projected lets a front-runner or prominent racer dictate from a position of comfort, reaching the turn fresh enough to repel challengers; Royal Poetry's course form over this type of trip makes it a prime beneficiary if the battle for the lead resolves itself cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running trio genuinely exhaust each other and the closers find clear daylight to deliver their runs approaching the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A proper pace meltdown leaves the lead vulnerable from two out, with any hold-up horse who has travelled smoothly through the race able to pick up the pieces; Molo Del Palazzo's placed efforts at this trip and Tipsy Tiger's record of finishing into the places under similar conditions make both credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Quickens Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce but not catastrophic, and a midfield runner times a run to split tiring horses inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Letmebetheboss or a well-positioned midfield runner finds a gap as the leaders stop in front of them and the hold-up horses arrive too late from the back; this is the least likely shape because it requires a very specific pace profile and precise riding from an apprentice jockey.

watchPoints.text: Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso will likely jostle aggressively for the lead inside the first two furlongs — watch for any one of them being checked or shuffled out of position, which could cause disruption for midfield runners tracking behind.

Dancing Tiger is the Strand scorecard top pick but is a genuine hold-up horse being compressed into a midfield position by the pace volume — watch whether Owen Lewis can find a clear run approaching the home turn, as traffic will be a real risk.

Plan C returns from 91 days off and is the least battle-hardened of the three front-runners — if it weakens sharply after halfway, it could unbalance the runners immediately behind, particularly Letmebetheboss and Molo Del Palazzo.

Tipsy Tiger's 74-day absence is the longest in the field — watch its behaviour in the preliminaries and its early position in running; if it travels sweetly through the pace, its placed form at this trip suggests it can stay involved, but fitness on return is genuinely uncertain.

Molo Del Palazzo holds the best recent placed form over this trip and going combination among the hold-up horses — watch how early Jack Dace commits for a run, as Sandown's flat finish rewards those who time their challenge precisely rather than kicking too soon or too late.
